mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial/company registry in the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., China SAMR or Hong Kong Companies Registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn German/French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority and notary public of the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certification or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the criminal record (Police Certificate) for each non-resident director or authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority of the holder's state of ordinary residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; translated by a Swiss court-licensed sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille; bank certified statement directed to the notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory baseline KYC under Art. 6 AMLA: verify identity of legal entity, all UBOs (24%+ direct/indirect ownership or control), and authorized signatories; screen against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, SECO sanctions ordinances (SR 946.211), EU restrictive measures aligned by Switzerland, OFAC SDN list where USD clearing is anticipated, and the FINMA enforcement databases. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) status under Art. 4 AMLA requires enhanced due diligence and senior management approval per FINMA Circular 2023/1. Simplified due diligence under Art. 3(2) AMLO-FINMA applies to a low-risk specialty grocery retail model provided that no PEP, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction indicators appear on any UBO, director, or source-of-funds review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), www.zefix.ch; operative name reservation is executed by the cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt) competent at the registered office, typically through the notary public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Per Art. 950 CO and Art. 65 HregV, the firm name must be truthful, not misleading, self-identifying as to legal form (AG or SA suffix mandatory), and may be in one of the four national official languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh). English or other foreign-language names are admissible only when customary, non-misleading, and accompanied by a clear Swiss nexus; script transliteration from Chinese characters is permissible solely as an unregistered trade description and cannot form the registered legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss, Schweizer, Suisse, Svizzera, Helvetia (used in a licensed or official sense)
Foundation, Stiftung, Fondation (requires foundation purpose and supervision)
Trust, Treuhand (requires financial intermediary license or professional trustee qualification)
Cantonal or municipal names and coat-of-arms terms (prior public authorization mandatory)
Terms implying regulated professions (doctor, lawyer, auditor, fiduciary) unless licensed
Military, police, Red Cross, and other government-exclusive emblems
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, obtain the written refusal from the cantonal commercial register office. File a formal written objection with the same office within 10 working days. If not remedied, lodge an administrative appeal (Beschwerde) with the cantonal supervisory authority within 30 days of the refusal decision under Art. 956 CO, followed, if necessary, by an appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court on federal-law grounds. In parallel, the notary may resubmit an amended name for a new preliminary search to avoid delaying the incorporation schedule.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole establishment address for this industry. Under Art. 626 para. 2 CO, the AG must hold a registered office in Switzerland at a place where administration can be verified; however, mandatory cantonal food-control registration under the Federal Foodstuffs Act (SR 817.0) and municipal business licensing require a physical retail store and storage premises, so the entity must demonstrate a real commercial lease at its registered address. A serviced-office or virtual seat may only supplement, not replace, the operational establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 95% likelihood of at least one unannounced cantonal food safety inspection (Kantonschemiker) within the first 6 months of operation; 60% likelihood of municipal trade-police and labor-compliance inspection in year 1; 10-15% likelihood of a corporate registered-office address verification by the commercial register during the incorporation year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/Code des Obligations), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft/stock corporation); Arts. 632 and 650 (minimum capital and partly paid shares), Art. 652 (formation procedure), Art. 627 (incorporators). New Swiss Company Law Reform in force since 1 January 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Federal Commercial Registry Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA) of the Swiss Federal Office of Justice, acting through the competent Cantonal Commercial Registry (Handelsregisteramt/Office du registre du commerce); public index administered via the Zefix portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Errichtungsakt/acte constitutif) containing the Articles of Association (Statuten/statuts), filed as an electronic registration application to the Cantonal Commercial Registry through the eGRIS/ePortal system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up, in no case less than CHF 50,000, deposited in a blocked capital payment account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank; written bank confirmation of the payment must be produced before registration (Art. 632 OR).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF ASIAN SUPERMARKET GROCERY HUB AG. The incorporators, sitting as the inaugural board, RESOLVE: (1) the Articles of Association are approved and the notarized deed of incorporation is ratified; (2) the subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100.00 nominal value each, is allotted to the subscribers; (3) the registered office is established at a lawful address in Zurich, Switzerland; (4) the appointment of the Managing Director and Chairman with individual signature authority is confirmed; (5) the officers are instructed to effect Commercial Registry registration, VAT and social insurance registration, and all food retail licensing; (6) the corporate seal is adopted and the minute book opened.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Swiss notary; submit the signed draft Articles of Association and the corporate name reservation confirmation obtained from Zefix; the notary verifies the identity, legal capacity and signatures of all incorporators, confirms the share capital and registered office provisions, and notarizes the public deed of incorporation. The certified deed becomes the basis for all subsequent registry and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certified passport or identity card copies of all incorporators
Signed Articles of Association (Statuten/statuts) in German or French
Zefix name reservation confirmation for 'Asian Supermarket Grocery Hub AG'
Draft deed of incorporation prepared by the notary
Declaration of subscription of the share capital
Registered office address confirmation/lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries any provision, the incorporators correct the Articles or add supplementary declarations; the deed is re-notarized at the notary's discretion, with no fresh governmental approval required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Share Capital into a Blocked Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss licensed bank (e.g., UBS AG, Credit Suisse AG, Raiffeisen, Zuger Kantonalbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital payment account (Sperrkonto) in the company's intended name; deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 nominal share capital; obtain a written bank confirmation certificate (Bankbestätigung) stating the account holder, deposit amount and blocking clause, to be released only on production of the Commercial Registry extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation extract
Passport copies of the subscribes
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration (UBO)
Bank account opening forms
Swiss residence or business address evidence of the signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deposit discrepancies or currency issues appear, the bank requests a corrective payment order or amended blocking instruction; a fresh confirmation certificate is issued on settlement without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing and Statutory Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Registry (Handelsregisteramt/Office du registre du commerce) under the supervisory oversight of the Federal Commercial Registry Office (EHRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application via eGRIS together with the notarized deed, bank confirmation, officer declarations and statutory signature cards; pay the cantonal and federal registration fees; the registry examines legal conformity, checks director disqualifications, and issues the legal entity status with the identification number (UID) upon entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
Bank confirmation of the CHF 50,000 paid-up capital
Declaration of the board members accepting office and confirming no bankruptcy/pending criminal records
Official signature cards of the officers
Completed registration form per the model of the Federal Commercial Registry Office
Payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice (Rechtsverzögerung), the notary files additional explanations or corrective annexes within the set deadline (usually 30 days); repeated failures trigger formal summons by EHRA for judicial direction, with an available appeal to the Cantonal Court of Appeals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT; Cantonal Social Insurance Office (AHV/AVS) for employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry entry, apply automatically for the canton tax file; submit a separate VAT registration declaration to the ESTV if annual taxable turnover will exceed CHF 100,000, which is mandatory for grocery retail; register as an employer with the Cantonal Compensation Office to obtain the AHV/AVS account number for payroll withholding.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry extract and UID number
Articles of Association
Notarized deed (for tax assessment of capital tax)
Lease agreement for the registered premises
Passport copies and residence permits of directors
Stock corporation tax questionnaire of the canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration numbers are not received or a query arises, the company submits corrections online via the tax authorities' e-services; retroactive adjustment of the VAT effective date is permissible upon demonstration of good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance and Operational Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss licensed bank and the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the operational current-account by converting the blocked capital payment account into the company's main account using the registry extract as release authority; issue share certificates to the subscribers; adopt the share register, minute book and financial year bookkeeping; file the explicit waiver of a statutory audit with the Commercial Registry if shareholders decide to forego a restricted audit under Art. 727a OR.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry extract showing legal personality
Board resolution authorizing account activation
List of shareholders and share certificates
Certified passports of the final authorized signatories
Waiver of the restricted audit (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account release, the board provides the missing corporate documents or clarification of the UBO declaration; a renewed release order is issued within the business day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Food Authorities (Kantonales Gewerbeinspektorat / Office cantonal de police du commerce) and the Cantonal Food Control Laboratory (Kantonales Laboratorium), supervised by the Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV/OSAV)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operating Registration (Lebensmittelbetriebsbewilligung / Autorisation d'établissement alimentaire) together with the Cantonal Commercial Activity Permit (Gewerbebewilligung) for retail grocery sales of imported Asian condiments and vegetables

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) and the competent Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'B' low-impact retail — screening under Art. 10a of the Swiss Environmental Protection Act (USG/LEp) determines that a full EIA Report is generally not required for a supermarket of this scale; a simple registration/screening form and environmental self-check suffice, unless floor space exceeds cantonal thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Art. 3 of the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV/OEaux) — no undiluted food waste or grease beyond BOD5/COD permit limits; refrigerated display cabinets must use F-gas compliant refrigerants per the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV) and the Ordinance on Fluorinated Greenhouse Gases; waste handling follows the Waste Ordinance (VVEA/OLED); noise from refrigeration and delivery units must stay within the planning values of the Noise Abatement Ordinance (LSV/OPB).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is issued by the Cantonal Fire Insurance Authority (VKF) after inspection of fire alarm systems, extinguishers and evacuation routes; structural load approval is granted by the municipal building inspectorate under the cantonal construction code confirming floor-load capacity of storage shelving; occupational safety clearance is effected through Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) covering employee safety training, and compliance with Art. 328 OR on protection of personal integrity and workplace accident prevention.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Administration fédérale des contributions (AFC) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration; principal portal: www.estv.admin.ch and SuisseTax e-filing platform; cantonal and communal tax authorities for profit and capital taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon commercial register entry, the Swiss AG obtains a unique UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) from the central UID register administered by the Federal Statistical Office. The UID is then used as the basis for the VAT number (CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST) after a separate VAT registration application is filed with ESTV using the official VAT registration form, submitted via SuisseTax or paper procedure. No additional corporate income TIN is separately issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Swiss AGs are subject to federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax on net profit as a separate taxable person; no pass-through doctrine applies; profits distributed to shareholders face Swiss federal withholding tax at 35% subject to treaty reduction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election and no elective hybrid-mismatch treatment in Swiss domestic law. Available elections include optional VAT group taxation among qualifying Swiss entities (Art. 120 LTVA) and, for direct taxes, election of tax consolidation (Steuergruppe / groupe fiscal) for qualifying wholly- or majority-owned Swiss group members. Anti-hybrid rules apply without elective carveouts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10 para. 2 LTVA, effective 1 January 2025, replacing the former CHF 100,000 threshold); voluntary registration may be requested below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoice stamping, or API clearance regime exists in Switzerland. VAT invoices may be issued electronically or on paper provided the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are preserved; Swiss QR-bill is a mandatory payment slip for certain B2B and B2C invoices but is not a tax clearance or fiscal-stamping obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are taxable at 0% where the goods physically leave Swiss customs territory to a foreign destination and the supplier holds contemporaneous evidence accepted by Swiss Customs (customs export declaration and transport documentation proving delivery abroad). Cross-border services are generally taxable in the customer's country if the customer is an entrepreneur abroad under Art. 18 LTVA; services physically or effectively supplied abroad may qualify for 0% rating. Zero-rating requires complete documentary proof and commercial invoices expressly allocating the Swiss 0% rate in the absence of an exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (e-dec or e-dec Web confirmation) discharged by the Swiss Federal Customs Administration in the exporter's name and EORI/UID reference
Transport document evidencing physical departure from Switzerland: CMR consignment note, bill of lading, air waybill, or postal/customs export receipt
Commercial supplier invoice stating 0% Swiss VAT with full supplier and purchaser identification and delivery terms
Supporting export evidence: foreign customs arrival documentation, warehouse release, or forwarder's proof of foreign destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Missing or contradictory export evidence triggers retrospective VAT adjustment at 8.1% with default surcharge and late-payment interest. Intentional or negligent misuse of export zero-rating constitutes tax evasion under Art. 104 LTVA, punishable by a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; fraudulent falsification of customs or transport documents may qualify as criminal tax fraud under Art. 106 LTVA with imprisonment and heavy fines. Swiss Customs penalties and ESTV clawback proceedings can run concurrently, and the taxpayer may be excluded from future zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and State Secretariat for International Financial Affairs (SIF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible. Switzerland maintains open capital and current accounts without quantitative exchange-control restrictions. Capital imports and exports, dividend remittances, interest payments, royalties, and loan repayments may be freely executed through licensed banks, subject only to Swiss corporate law solvency tests, contractual obligations, and the 35% federal withholding tax on distributions unless reduced under an applicable double-taxation treaty. There is no foreign-investment licensing regime for ordinary importing and retail operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Swiss law imposes no mandatory conversion or surrender timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may retain receivables in foreign currency or convert them freely through the interbank market. The only statutory obligations are SNB statistical reporting for balance-of-payments and direct-investment data and general tax/booking documentation. For an import-led grocery retail entity there is no relevant surrender obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Restricted / Conditional. Offshore electronic-money institutions are not a viable primary treasury rail because they cannot hold statutory capital escrow balances, provide documentary letter-of-credit services, or access the Swiss SIC clearing system. A FINMA-licensed Swiss fintech with a banking or fintech license may support e-money and payment initiation as a supplementary channel, but all high-value treasury operations must remain with a regulated Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video identification is legally accepted under FINMA Circular 2016/07 and Swiss AMLA delegation rules. In practice, tier-1 commercial banks frequently require a physical compliance interview for directors and beneficial owners, especially when non-resident shareholders are involved. The prudent onboarding assumption is that at least one director must appear at a Swiss branch or a recognized Swiss embassy/notary for biometric verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure in beneficial ownership or trade counterparty structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and proofs of residence for all ultimate beneficial owners; notarized source-of-wealth statement and CV; commercial registration extracts for the AG and all parent entities; negative hits report from World-Check and MATCH; an audited financial statement or opening balance sheet; a reference letter from a FINMA/SNB-licensed external bank; and a clear organizational chart evidencing the full ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear origin of capital intended for the AG's share capital deposit or shareholder loan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share-subscription deed or capital-increase resolution; original bank statements from the remitting financial institution; signed source-of-funds declaration covering sale of goods, director savings, or family gifts; tax residence certificates; valid shareholder loan agreement with commercial terms; and a written confirmation that no cryptocurrency or untraceable funds were used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing from a non-resident shareholder to the Swiss AG is executed by SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary name matching the AG commercial register entry and the remittance purpose coded as 'Capital contribution / shareholder loan'. Funds are settled through SIC for CHF and TARGET2 for EUR. The receiving bank requires a notarized copy of the incorporation deed or capital-increase resolution, a completed source-of-funds questionnaire, and corporate authorization documentation. Standard clearing and AML verification may take up to 10 business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for imported Asian grocery stock are made by SWIFT MT103 for open-account trade, while documentary credits under UCP600 remain the preferred clearing rail for bulk shipments with transport, phyto-sanitary, and customs documentation. Domestic Swiss franc vendor payments clear through SIC, euro disbursements route via TARGET2, and cross-currency payments are converted through the executing bank's FX desk. All outbound payments require matching invoices, packing lists, import permits, and food-safety certificates to satisfy bank compliance and Switzerland's Sanitary and Phytosanitary regime.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards with Swiss or G20-regulated counterparties for covered exposures up to 12 months
Cross-currency swaps aligning GBP/EUR/CHF liabilities with Asian import-payable tenors
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for minor Asian currencies lacking onshore deliverability, such as IDR and VND

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting: approval of annual financial statements, profit appropriation, and discharge of board; signed minutes maintained in corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate action; minutes kept at registered office; any resulting director, auditor, or capital changes filed separately with the Cantonal Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); court-appointed extension possible
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic strike-off; shareholders may sue to compel the meeting; managing directors may be liable for damages if non-convening causes loss

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return with annual financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (Steueramt / Administration cantonale des impôts) for corporate income and capital tax; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) receives the direct federal tax through cantonal assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonally set, generally six months after fiscal year end; extension available on reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest; late-filing procedural fine; estimated assessment; tax-evasion penalty up to three times the tax evaded; no direct administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss value added tax return for taxable sales, input VAT deduction, and VAT liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of each tax period; quarterly reporting is standard for VAT-liable businesses with taxable turnover above CHF 100,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at the statutory rate (currently 4.5%); procedural penalties up to CHF 5,000; tax-evasion penalty up to three times the amount evaded; enforcement under debt collection law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration and social security contributions (AHV/IV/EO/ALV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse / caisse de compensation) designated for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Contributions are payable with each payroll; annual wage declaration filed in the first calendar quarter of the following year (exact date set by the compensation office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on arrears; late-declaration surcharge; personal liability of directors for unpaid employer social security contributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register data maintenance: confirmation that registered office, directors, auditors, and signatory powers remain current; notification of any changes without delay
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; changes must be registered promptly after the underlying shareholder or board decision; no fixed annual filing exists for unchanged data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cantonal procedural fines for late or incomplete registration; if the company becomes unreachable or lacks a valid legal address, the Commercial Register may, after formal warning, initiate administrative strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit applies to an AG that is subject to Swiss or foreign securities listing, has outstanding public bonds, or exceeds any two of the following thresholds in two consecutive years: CHF 20 million balance-sheet total, CHF 40 million net turnover, 250 annual full-time employees. Simplified audit applies to all other AGs unless shareholders unanimously decide to dispense with the audit, an option available only if the AG has an annual average of not more than 10 full-time employees and no ordinary audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts under Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958–963g CO); Swiss GAAP FER for further reporting; IFRS required for most listed issuers on SIX and permitted as a substitute for statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss AG law does not impose an annual public confirmation solely for shareholding transfers. Transfers of registered shares are entered in the company's internal share register upon notification; bearer-share beneficial owners must be recorded in the statutory beneficial-owner register under CO Art. 697i. Beneficial-owner data must be disclosed to tax and AML authorities on request, and any material change is updated without delay in the internal corporate records. Any central transparency- or UBO-register reporting obligation follows an on-change trigger rather than an annual calendar filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (internal mandates and Commercial Register data)
Register of Beneficial Owners of bearer shares, if bearer shares are issued (CO Art. 697i)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450–1,200 per year for Swiss registered-office and corporate-secretarial services, depending on canton and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–7,500 for a simplified audit; USD 12,000–45,000 for an ordinary audit; USD 0 if shareholders validly opt out

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal flat rate on post-tax profit, i.e. 7.83% effective on pre-tax profit under the Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax (DBG/IFD); plus cantonal and communal profit taxes of approx. 7.0–16.0%, yielding a combined effective rate of approx. 11.9% (Zug) to 21.1% (Geneva) depending on the registered seat.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal statutory tax holidays are not available for supermarket retail. Preferential instruments: (i) participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug, DBG Art. 69) exempting qualifying substantial dividend income and capital gains; (ii) patent box (max. 90% relief on qualifying IP income) and (iii) R&D super-deduction limited to 50% of actual research costs (STAF cantonal measures); (iv) notional interest deduction on excess capital in participating cantons (Zug, Zurich). A physically present food retail business normally cannot use patent-box or NID; only participation relief may apply where the Swiss AG holds Asian group subsidiaries.
